title: A flat rotation curve needs dark matter
caption: If a galaxy's mass were all in its visible disc, orbital speeds beyond the disc would fall as 1/√r (dashed). Instead they stay flat at about 200 km s⁻¹. Then M(r) = v²r/G grows in proportion to r: unseen mass keeps adding up, with density falling as 1/r².
alt: Orbital speed against radius: an observed flat line at 200 kilometres per second, and a dashed Keplerian curve falling from 200 at 8 kiloparsecs to 100 at 32.
description: Observed: v ≈ 200 km s⁻¹ out to large radius.
Expected from visible mass alone (beyond 8 kpc): v = 200√(8/r), half as fast at 32 kpc.
Flat v means M(r) = v²r/G ∝ r: a halo of dark matter with ρ ∝ 1/r².
